nodes.label: Three validators, one Diagnostic type
nodes.rationale: saxes for well-formedness during parse, libxml2 via WASM in a worker debounced ~150ms, and the fontoxpath Schematron interpreter — all emitting the same shape so the Problems panel, tree badges and explainer have exactly one thing to render. The guidance engine is an explicitly advisory fourth source.

nodes.label: XsdEngine interface
nodes.rationale: libxml2-wasm primary with xmllint-wasm as a named fallback behind one interface — same underlying C library, so switching is a driver swap rather than a rewrite. libxml2-wasm is preferred for its reusable compiled-schema handle, since xmlSchemaParse dominates cost in an interactive edit loop.

nodes.label: Explicit disposal of native-memory handles in the worker
nodes.rationale: A leak here is a wasm heap OOM, not a GC pause; ownership lives entirely in the worker, one handle per schema set, disposed on schema change.

nodes.label: libxml2 demoted from authoritative validator to fast 1.0 oracle
nodes.rationale: libxml2 implements XML Schema 1.0 only and the maintainer has stated 1.1 is not planned; there is no JavaScript alternative, and Saxon-EE is a commercial per-seat Java product with no browser story.

nodes.label: XSD version detection prefers 1.1 when ambiguous
nodes.rationale: Detection comes from vc:minVersion/vc:maxVersion and from the presence of 1.1-only constructs; when ambiguous prefer 1.1 because it is the superset, and say which version was assumed.

nodes.label: Resolve the schema graph in JavaScript before calling into WASM
nodes.rationale: libxml2 will happily compile a schema with unresolved imports and then validate against the partial model, silently under-reporting errors — a correctness failure that looks like success. So walk the closure, resolve through the catalogue, rewrite to flat filenames, materialise into the WASM virtual FS, and assert the closure is complete.

nodes.label: ValidationPayload with lineMap
nodes.rationale: One element start-tag per line makes 'error at line 42' an O(1) exact lookup. This serialisation is only for validation and never written to disk, so it does not conflict with the lossless splice serializer. The rejected alternative — injecting tracking attributes — looks correct in a prototype and then fails against any strict schema with cvc-complex-type.3.2.2, because the injected attributes are themselves invalid.

nodes.label: Revision tagging and terminate-and-respawn cancellation
nodes.rationale: A transparent proxy hides exactly the lifecycle control needed, which is why the protocol is hand-rolled rather than Comlink; in-flight results render dimmed rather than cleared so the UI never flickers through a misleading 'no problems' state mid-edit.

nodes.label: IDomFacade: our CST is the XPath data model
nodes.rationale: No second DOM, no sync problem, no serialisation round-trip.

nodes.label: First-match-wins per context node
nodes.rationale: Within a pattern a node is claimed by the first rule whose context matches it and later rules do not fire. This is the semantic beginners trip over most, hence the shadowing detector.

nodes.label: @context is an XSLT match pattern, not an XPath expression
nodes.rationale: Prefixing descendant-or-self::node()/ unless it starts with / is correct for essentially all real-world contexts but diverges on predicates in certain positions; document the approximation and test it.

nodes.label: queryBinding semantic drift
nodes.rationale: Running an xslt (XPath 1.0) schema under 3.1 keeps general comparisons existential but changes untyped string-vs-number comparisons, so warn on queryBinding="xslt".

nodes.label: Foreign XSLT in Schematron: detect and refuse explicitly
nodes.rationale: xsl:function, xsl:key, xsl:template and EXSLT cannot run on this interpreter, and some real healthcare and DITA Schematron uses them. Silently mis-validating is far worse than declining.

nodes.label: Live rule testing — the killer beginner feature
nodes.rationale: Context match counts, per-rule fire counts, shadowing detection, per-assertion pass/fail lists and message preview with sch:value-of interpolated. It exists because the interpreter was chosen over the compiled pipeline, and it is what turns Schematron from an expert-only format into something a beginner can iterate on.

nodes.label: Compiled-expression cache and single-walk pattern evaluation
nodes.rationale: Naive evaluation is O(patterns x rules x nodes); mitigate with a cache keyed on (expression, namespaceBindings) using compileXPathToJavaScript, and evaluate patterns in one document walk rather than one traversal per rule.

nodes.label: The anti-drift differential harness
nodes.rationale: The guidance engine and the authoritative validators are independent implementations; disagreement means the product teaches beginners wrong things, which is worse than being merely buggy. Publish the pass rate — a number in CI output is the only thing that stops 'the engine works' from quietly becoming untrue.

nodes.label: SchXslt2 + xslt3 as the CI-only Schematron oracle
nodes.rationale: Never shipped to the browser; it targets ISO/IEC 19757-3:2025 and covers all but one feature of it, so our interpreter should target the same edition rather than the older 2016/2020 texts.

nodes.label: A .sch someone emailed you is executable code
nodes.rationale: Classical Schematron compiles to Turing-complete XSLT with fn:doc(), fn:unparsed-text() and xsl:result-document, so a malicious rule can exfiltrate the whole document with the user's network position and cookies — including Schematron embedded in xs:appinfo, which the user never consciously chose to run. The fontoxpath interpreter is safe by construction, a second independent justification for the interpreter decision.

nodes.label: If XSLT ever becomes necessary: null-origin sandboxed iframe
nodes.rationale: sandbox="allow-scripts" without allow-same-origin, under Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none', communicating by postMessage, with a Playwright test asserting zero network egress during validation.

nodes.label: libxml2 parser flag policy
nodes.rationale: Always XML_PARSE_NONET; never NOENT, DTDLOAD, DTDATTR, XINCLUDE or HUGE. NOENT expands external entities and DTDLOAD fetches them, and libxml2's billion-laughs check is disabled by HUGE — exactly the flag someone turns on the first time a large document fails to parse.

nodes.label: Never auto-fetch a remote schemaLocation
nodes.rationale: A named rule in the plan precisely because it is the most likely place someone adds a convenience fetch() six months in; the user sees the full URL and decides.

nodes.label: One resolver, one choke point (src/io/resolver.ts)
nodes.rationale: Serves only buffers already in the in-app catalogue and every other URI returns not-found, which makes the no-fetch guarantee reviewable in one file rather than auditable across a codebase.

nodes.label: No telemetry in v1
nodes.rationale: An enforceable promise because there is no server to send anything to; the optional CORS proxy fetches only schemas the user explicitly asked for and never sees document content.
